comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's server CPU portfolio includes the EPYC Series, based on x86 architecture for high-performance computing and large data centers, with the recent announcement of the 5th generation AMD EPYC family.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose the launch and ramp of their latest 5th generation server CPU families for data centers in 2024. Intel launched the Intel Xeon 6 processors using the Intel 3 process and Efficient cores, while also ramping its 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors based on Intel 7. Similarly, AMD announced its 5th generation AMD EPYC family of server processors, expanding its high-performance server CPU portfolio. Both disclosures highlight the strategic introduction of new generation processors to address diverse data center workloads.

sentences.text: ▪Data center CPUs. We launched our Intel® Xeon® 6 processors for the data center, utilizing the Intel 3 process, including our first Intel Xeon processor using Efficient cores (E-cores). The Intel Xeon 6 family is designed to address the growing diversity in workloads and deployments in the data center environments. Our 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, were launched in 2023, and continued to ramp throughout 2024.
We recently announced our 5th generation AMD EPYC family of server processors, further expanding our high-performance server CPU portfolio.
